subject: Urgent: zone partition impacting EU & APAC — recommended reroute and post-incident plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: zone partition impacting EU & APAC — recommended reroute and post-incident plan

Hi Alice,

We wanted to notify you immediately: starting ~09:00 UTC we observed a cloud provider network partition that is affecting a subset of our serving capacity in EU and APAC regions. Some API requests from your EU and APAC user base are seeing increased tail latency and intermittent failures (5xx). US regions are not affected.

What we recommend right now:
- Short term (minutes): Route EU traffic to our nearby EU standby cluster in eu-west-1 (automatic prefix redirection). We can perform this flip for you if you approve.
- Short term (minutes): For APAC, we recommend a regional failover to ap-southeast-1 with the per-route fallback policy enabled (will increase latency by ~80–120ms for affected users).
- Monitoring: We will hold a 15-minute war room and keep you updated.

Attachments: traffic-shift-runbook.pdf (step-by-step), reroute-diagram.png (visual).

Please reply with permission to proceed on the above flips and whether you want us to do EU and APAC at the same time or stagger them (we usually stagger by region to reduce cache-warmup impact).

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your checkout flow during peak hours. We'll follow up with a timeline and incident ticket (INF-7421).

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

--

2) Can you confirm whether session affinity / KV cache will be preserved after the flip or whether we should expect some cold-cache behavior?

If you need a quick call I can join the war room — I'm available 09:40–10:30 UTC.

Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: zone partition impacting EU & APAC — recommended reroute and post-incident plan

Tessa / Connor,

Status update from SRE: root cause appears to be a peering misconfiguration at the cloud vendor's regional edge — some prefixes are being dropped into a blackhole between eu-central-1 and several control-plane endpoints. Impact window currently unknown; cloud has acknowledged and opened an internal high-priority ticket.

Planned actions (we can execute now for Acme if Tessa has approval):
- Execute EU flip: set route target -> eu-west-1 standby pool, enable graceful drain (30s) and redirect for inbound requests. This requires no customer DNS or TLS changes — the endpoint is the same hostname and certificate; traffic is routed at our edge.
- Cache behavior: prefix/KV cache will not be preserved across the pool (we will warm caches aggressively using synthetic priming for your top 50 prompt keys). Expect a brief cold-cache window ~2–5 minutes where per-request cost/latency increases.
- APAC: recommend hold until we confirm cloud-side mitigation or do staged flip to ap-southeast-1 (we can do both in sequence).

I'll standby for —Approve EU flip now —Approve EU+APAC staged flips

Connor, can you prepare the synthetic prime list and a quick dashboard (top prompts + cache hit rate) so we can monitor post-flip?

Dylan
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: zone partition (EU/APAC) — impact, mitigation, and next steps

Alice, Dylan, Connor —

Thanks for your patience. This is the post-incident follow-up for the zone partition that affected a subset of EU and APAC capacity on 2026-07-07. Summary below; attached is the postmortem draft for your review (postmortem-draft.docx).

What happened:
- At ~09:00 UTC a peering configuration error in the cloud provider caused intermittent reachability between control-plane endpoints and a portion of our regional edge network. This caused elevated 5xx rates for customers whose traffic routed through the impacted edge nodes.

Customer impact for Acme Retail:
- EU: elevated 5xx and increased checkout latency for ~18 minutes. We performed an emergency flip to eu-west-1 at 10:08 UTC; successful cutover completed ~10:12 UTC. Checkout availability recovered within 6 minutes after priming.
- APAC: some requests experienced increased latency but we avoided a full immediate flip; we executed a staged flip to ap-southeast-1 at 11:05 UTC after cloud confirmed partial mitigation. Total APAC impact window ~95 minutes with degraded latency for ~45 minutes.

Mitigation and why it worked:
- Standby pools and automatic route target policies allowed us to move traffic without cert/DNS changes.
- Aggressive cache priming reduced the cold-cache period to ~2–5 minutes, limiting sustained error rates.

Actions we are taking (next 30 days):
- Change control: require pre-deployment peering checks on vendor side and an automated probe suite to detect blackhole prefixes. (INF-7432)
- Faster priming: add an on-demand pre-warm API for our customers to trigger priming for critical prompt sets. (RFC in progress)
- SLA buffer: offering Acme Retail a one-month service credit for the incident window; I'll loop in finance for formal approval.

Files attached: postmortem-draft.docx (draft), traffic-shift-runbook.pdf (finalized steps), reroute-diagram.png.

If you'd like any change to the postmortem wording or additional telemetry included, please reply with specific asks and we'll incorporate them. We're scheduling a 30-minute retrospective next week if you'd like to join.

Apologies again for the disruption — we recognize the impact during a peak hour and appreciate your collaboration in the war room.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
